findings.fix: Add `method="POST" action="/api/register"` (or appropriate endpoint) to the form tag.
findings.violation: The form is missing `method` and `action` attributes, so it cannot submit properly or securely (missing method defaults to GET, which is insecure for password fields).
The select element is missing a `name` attribute, so the selected shipping speed will not be submitted with the form.

findings.fix: Add `value` attributes to each option: `<option value="standard">Standard</option>`, `<option value="express">Express</option>`, etc.
findings.violation: The option elements lack `value` attributes, so the form will submit the display text instead of consistent internal values.

findings.evidence: `<label id="name-label" for="name-input">Full name</label>` and `<label id="legalname-label" for="legalname-input">Your name</label>`
findings.fix: Remove one of the duplicate fields, or if both are genuinely needed, clarify their distinct purposes with labels like "Full name (for login)" and "Legal name (for billing)".
findings.location: Full name and legal name fields, lines 10 and 56
findings.violation: The form asks for "Full name" and then separately for "Your name" (legal name), requesting the same information twice and confusing users about which to fill.

findings.evidence: `placeholder="Must be 8 digits"` with no `maxlength` or `pattern` attribute
findings.fix: Add `maxlength="8" pattern="[0-9]{8}"` to enforce the 8-digit requirement.
findings.violation: The label and placeholder promise an 8-digit constraint, but the input has no validation to enforce it, allowing invalid entries.

findings.fix: Change to `type="time"` for a time picker, or use a `<select>` element if only predefined time slots are acceptable.
findings.violation: The field is labeled "Preferred contact time" but uses type="text", which provides no validation, appropriate mobile keyboard, or time-picker UI.

findings.fix: Remove the inline style and define label styling in a CSS file instead.

findings.fix: Either remove the button if not needed, or add an `onclick` handler and corresponding JavaScript to reveal the intended details.
